headline: Snap pitches itself as a kind, creative, purpose-driven camera company — but its careers copy shrank sharply after 2022, muting nearly every signal.
identity: Snap has consistently valued kindness, creativity, and intellectual curiosity, anchoring its copy across all years to the trio 'We Are Kind / Creative / Smart' and the mission line 'contribute to human progress by empowering people to express themselves.' DEI and inclusion language surged from near-absent in 2018 to a peak in 2020–2021 — with explicit terms like 'LGBTQ+,' 'unconscious bias training,' and 'allyship' — then retreated sharply by 2022–2023, with 'bias' and 'lgbtq' disappearing from the copy after 2021 and the 2023 careers page reduced to a thin handful of chunks dominated by the peer-support 'Snap-a-Wish' program. The altruism z-score dropped to –2.14 in 2023, the lowest in the dataset, signaling a dramatic pullback in the breadth of self-description.
fit: You might be a good fit if you are someone who 'thinks deeply, questions conventions, and strives to never stop learning,' values empathy as a workplace norm ('listen from the heart'), and is comfortable with a company whose public identity has become noticeably leaner and less elaborated since 2022.

sections.heading: Core Identity: Kind, Creative, Smart
sections.body:
From 2018 onward, Snap's careers copy has returned to the same three value pillars in nearly every year: 'We Are Kind,' 'We Are Creative,' and 'We Are Smart.' The phrasing evolved slightly — by 2021 'Kind' became 'operate with courage, show empathy, and instill trust through honesty and integrity,' and 'Smart' became 'solve problems through action, make high-quality decisions, and think with a strategic mindset' — but the three-part structure held.

The overarching mission statement, 'We contribute to human progress by empowering people to express themselves, live in the moment, learn about the world, and have fun together,' appeared verbatim in every year from 2018 through at least 2022, making it the single most stable piece of copy in the dataset. Techno-optimism scores were low throughout and turned negative by 2022–2023, meaning the copy does not lean on technology-as-salvation rhetoric; the camera framing is present but understated.

sections.heading: DEI Arc: Expansion 2020–2021, Then Retreat
sections.body:
In 2018, the DEI facet registered zero chunks in any explicit demographic or structural register — the page had no dedicated inclusion section. By 2020, a full 'Diversity, Equity & Inclusion' section appeared, and inclusion z-scores jumped to +1.21 (2020) and +1.28 (2021), well above peers. The copy named specific axes — 'race, gender, LGBTQ+, disability, age, socio-economic status, parental status, cognitive diversity, regional diversity' — and described concrete programs: 'unconscious bias training, allyship training, networking opportunities, recruiting initiatives.' The phrase 'DEI is everyone's job because it fuels creative excellence and innovation' framed inclusion as a performance argument, not just a values statement.

By 2022 the aspirational_vague register dropped to zero chunks, 'bias' and 'lgbtq' vanished from the lexicon, and the inclusion z-score fell to +0.31. In 2023 the inclusion score collapsed to –1.76 and the page was flagged as thin (3 chunks), with the top-scoring inclusion quotes coming only from the peer-support 'Snap-a-Wish' blurb. The employee resource groups (SnapNoir, SnapFamilia, SnapAsia, SnapAbility, SnapVets, Kaleidoscope) continued to appear in list form in 2023, but without the surrounding programmatic language that characterized 2020–2021.

sections.heading: 2023 and the Thin-Page Caveat
sections.body:
Multiple facets flag 2023 as 'thin' — only 3 chunks of careers copy were captured, versus 22–30 in peak years. This means the 2023 z-scores (altruism –2.14, mission_rights –2.44, meritocracy –2.01, performance –1.88) likely reflect a stripped-down page rather than a deliberate ideological shift, and should be read cautiously. The data beyond 2023 is truncated ('…+3 more' years), so the most recent trajectory is not fully visible here.

What is clear is that between 2021 and 2023 the careers copy became substantially shorter and less elaborated across every measured dimension — inclusion, performance, altruism, wellbeing, and mission language all declined together. Whether that reflects a page redesign, a content strategy change, or something else cannot be determined from this data alone.
